scams.name: Train Station Luggage Helper Theft
scams.description: Organized groups of thieves operate at Colmar train station, posing as helpful strangers offering to assist tourists with their luggage. Two or three young individuals approach travelers on stairs or near platforms, insisting on helping carry bags despite refusals. While one person distracts with conversation or blocks your view, another rifles through bags or pockets, stealing passports, wallets, and valuables.
scams.avoidance: Firmly decline all unsolicited help with luggage. Ask station staff in red tabards for assistance if needed. Keep bags zipped and secured in front of your body. Travel with only luggage you can manage alone.
scams.location: Colmar train station (Gare de Colmar), platform stairs, luggage areas

scams.name: Christmas Market Pickpocketing
scams.description: During Colmar's famous Christmas markets (late November through December), professional pickpockets work the dense crowds moving between market stalls. Victims often report having wallets stolen from zipped crossbody purses or coat pockets while navigating the narrow medieval streets packed with holiday shoppers. The crush of tourists photographing half-timbered houses creates perfect cover for skilled thieves.
scams.avoidance: Wear crossbody bags in front of your body with locking zippers. Keep wallets in front pockets or money belts under clothing. Visit markets Monday-Thursday when crowds are lighter. Avoid peak weekend hours between 11am-5pm.
scams.location: Colmar Christmas Markets, Place des Dominicains, Place de l'Ancienne Douane, Petite Venise, medieval Old Town pedestrian streets

scams.name: Restaurant Tourist Menu Overcharging
scams.description: Certain restaurants in Colmar's heavily-touristed areas engage in deceptive pricing practices. Visitors have reported being charged 7 euros extra per person when attempting to share a menu. Other tactics include presenting tourists with different menus featuring inflated prices, adding undisclosed charges for bread or water, or bringing unrequested items and billing for them.
scams.avoidance: Check prices on posted menus before sitting down. Eat where locals eat - venture a few streets from main tourist paths. Review recent TripAdvisor and Google reviews before dining. Ask for itemized bill and verify all charges match menu prices.
scams.location: Little Venice (Petite Venise), Place de l'Ancienne Douane, Rue des Marchands, areas near Maison Pfister

scams.name: Fake Petition/Deaf Charity Scam
scams.description: Groups of individuals approach tourists with clipboards, asking them to sign petitions for fake charitable causes, often pretending to be deaf-mute. The petitions are typically in English (suspicious in a French city) and claim to support disabled people. After signing, they reveal a 'donation' column and pressure you for 10-20 euros. While you're distracted, an accomplice may be pickpocketing you.
scams.avoidance: Say 'Non, merci' firmly and keep walking without stopping. Never sign anything offered by strangers on the street. Keep your bag secured in front of you if approached. Remember that legitimate charities don't solicit cash on streets.
scams.location: Colmar train station area, Place Rapp, near Musee Unterlinden, Cathedral of Saint Martin, tourist walking areas

scams.name: ATM Skimming and Card Fraud
scams.description: France experiences 42% of all European bank card fraud. Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs that capture card data and hidden cameras or keypad overlays that record PIN entries. Tourist areas are prime targets because foreign cards are less likely to have advanced security features. Victims typically discover the theft weeks later when unauthorized charges appear on their statements.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours only. Inspect the card slot and keypad before inserting card - wiggle the slot. Always cover your hand when entering PIN. Set up transaction alerts on your cards before traveling.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs in tourist areas, train station ATMs, ATMs on Rue des Marchands, machines near Christmas markets

scams.name: Fake Police Officer Scam
scams.description: Scammers pose as plainclothes police officers, quickly flashing fake badges and demanding to 'check your documents and wallet for counterfeit currency.' While examining your wallet, they palm cash or memorize card details. Some wear partial uniforms or hats with police markings to appear legitimate. French authorities have warned about increased incidents of criminals impersonating officers.
scams.avoidance: Know that real French police will NEVER demand your wallet, cash, or phone. Ask to see proper identification and request their serial number. Suggest going to the nearest police station together for any document checks. Call 17 (police emergency) if unsure about legitimacy.
scams.location: Colmar train station, parking areas near Old Town, near tourist attractions, quiet side streets

scams.name: QR Code Parking Meter Scam (Quishing)
scams.description: Scammers place fake QR code stickers over legitimate ones on parking meters throughout France. When tourists scan the fraudulent code, they're directed to a convincing phishing website that mimics official parking payment services. Victims enter their license plate, parking duration, and credit card details - all captured by criminals. Some victims are tricked into entering multiple card numbers after being told their payment 'failed.'
scams.avoidance: Run your finger over QR codes to detect if it's a sticker covering another code. Type parking payment URLs directly rather than scanning codes. Use official parking apps downloaded from app stores, not QR links. Pay at meter using coin or chip-enabled card rather than QR when possible.
scams.location: Public parking meters throughout Colmar, parking areas near Old Town, tourist parking zones

scams.name: Wine Tasting Pressure Sales
scams.description: While wine tastings along the Alsace Wine Route often appear free, there's strong social pressure to purchase bottles afterward. Some establishments serve generous pours to lower inhibitions, create false scarcity ('last bottles of this vintage'), or make tourists feel obligated after extensive tastings. Staff may become noticeably cold or hostile if visitors don't make purchases.
scams.avoidance: Look for 'Vignobles et Decouvertes' certified wineries for quality assurance. Set a budget before entering any cave and stick to it. Know it's perfectly acceptable to taste and buy just one bottle or none at all. Ask about tasting fees upfront before sampling begins.
scams.location: Alsace Wine Route villages (Eguisheim, Riquewihr, Kaysersberg), small caves in Colmar, roadside tasting rooms

scams.name: Rental Car Break-In Theft
scams.description: Thieves specifically target rental cars parked at tourist attractions throughout Alsace. They watch parking lots for tourists who open their trunks to store or retrieve items, marking which vehicles contain valuables. Rental cars are easily identified by registration stickers, missing floor mats, and clean interiors. Travelers return from wine tastings to find windows smashed and all belongings stolen.
scams.avoidance: Never open your trunk in the parking lot where thieves might see contents. Retrieve needed items a mile before arriving at destination. Remove all visible items including guidebooks, maps, and ticket stubs. Use underground or multistorey car parks with CCTV when possible.
scams.location: Tourist parking areas along Wine Route, parking lots at village viewpoints, free parking zones near attractions, trailhead parking

scams.name: Fake Accommodation Booking Scam
scams.description: Scammers create fake listings mimicking real Colmar properties on platforms like Airbnb and Booking.com, or send phishing emails claiming your reservation was cancelled with large penalty charges. Colmar's picturesque half-timbered houses make it easy to steal photos for convincing fake listings. Victims arrive to find their 'charming Alsatian apartment' doesn't exist.
scams.avoidance: Book only through official platforms and pay within their secure system. Verify emails by logging into booking sites directly, never via email links. Cross-reference property photos using reverse image search. Read reviews carefully and look for specific details about Colmar location.
scams.location: Online platforms, fake booking websites, phishing emails
